tasks.short: Hire, train and evaluate postal employees

steps.what: Hire and train employees and evaluate performance through evidence review and direct discussion

tasks.design: Keep hiring judgment, practical training and performance discussions with the manager, using {HCM} and {DOCS} for existing records. No automated candidate ranking, performance score or employee decision is introduced.
tasks.previous_blocker: Staff decisions depend on evidence, context and direct discussion.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing personnel records support accountable management.
tasks.still_hard: Fair interpretation of incomplete evidence and useful feedback.
tasks.human_edge: The manager hears employee perspectives and explains decisions.

reach.learn: Separate observed evidence from assumptions about a person

evidence.claim: Manual staffing and coaching are an E1 design; shift-planning cases do not establish savings in these personnel judgments.

assumptions: This task covers general employees; associate-unit manager selection and training are assigned separately.
The manager gathers evidence and employee perspectives within s1 with all time retained; no free performance or suitability score is assumed.
Existing HCM and DOCS precede any new tool.
No new service or incremental upkeep is introduced.
unknowns: Local staffing authority and current personnel process
research_questions: Is there recurring personnel administration distinct from hiring, coaching and evaluation?

already_counted.description: Evidence review, staffing judgment, practical training and feedback

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 R=100 gives zero gross and net saving. No clerical hiring component is invented.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare and submit postal activity reports

steps.what: Verify post office activity figures and capture reporting context
Prepare detailed and summary reports using configured tables and totals
Resolve reporting exceptions, add explanations and submit reports to designated supervisors

tasks.design: Configure native activity tables and report templates in {OPS_SYSTEM} and {BI}. The manager verifies the source dataset, writes contextual explanation and checks the exact report before submitting through {EMAIL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated table assembly and copying into detailed and summary reports.
tasks.enabler_now: Native report definitions can reproduce checked figures without a model.
tasks.still_hard: Inconsistent activity definitions and explanations that the numbers do not establish.
tasks.human_edge: The manager explains operational causes and challenges misleading totals.

reach.learn: Keep report totals traceable to consistent source definitions

evidence.claim: Configured activity reports are a proposed deterministic E1 approach; no measured postal report automation case is supplied.

assumptions: This task prepares reports; collecting mail, operating counters and staffing decisions remain outside the saving.

In s1 the manager produces reporting period, unit identifier, measure definitions, checked counts, source references and context notes; 35 hours include capture and reconciliation. Missing or conflicting totals require manual correction in s3.
Native OPS_SYSTEM reports and BI templates precede custom software or model commentary.
The report service does not infer operational causes from figures or send reports autonomously.
research_questions: Can configured outputs reproduce a checked reporting period while reducing actual table assembly time?

already_counted.description: Source verification, capture, explanation and final report review

incremental.description: Maintain measure definitions and audit report reconciliation
Support report access and data mapping integrity

approvals.approved_version: Exact report period, figures, explanation and recipient list; changes require manager review

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 R=65 gives 35 gross less 7 focal upkeep =28 central net. Report 0-5 pending assembly timing; existing reports or source reconciliation can remove the gain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Negotiate labor disputes through evidence review, dialogue and agreed settlement boundaries

tasks.design: Retain labour negotiation with the manager and the relevant parties, using {DOCS} for agreed evidence and proposals. No automated concession, settlement or assessment of intent is introduced.
tasks.previous_blocker: Resolution depends on trust, competing interests and the parties' authority.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing records support direct evidence-based discussion.
tasks.still_hard: Finding terms that are acceptable, feasible and within authority.
tasks.human_edge: The manager listens, clarifies interests and takes responsibility for proposals.

reach.learn: Clarify authority and distinguish positions from underlying concerns

evidence.claim: Manual labour negotiation is an E1 design; the digest establishes no measured replacement of bargaining.

assumptions: The baseline is negotiation, not a separate document-summarization service.
The manager obtains concerns, perspectives and authority clarification within s1 with all time retained.
Existing DOCS and direct dialogue precede new tools.
No new service or incremental upkeep is introduced; proposals do not automatically bind any party.
research_questions: What evidence or authority uncertainty most often delays a negotiation?

already_counted.description: Review evidence, hear parties and negotiate proposals

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 R=100; gross and net saving zero. No unsupported summarization or bargaining reduction is assumed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Select and train associate-unit postal managers

steps.what: Select postmasters and associate-unit managers and train them through practical management coaching

tasks.design: Keep associate-unit manager selection and coaching with the postal manager, using existing {HCM} records and {DOCS} learning material. This manager population is excluded from the general employee task's proposed scope.
tasks.previous_blocker: Manager suitability and development depend on unit needs and direct evidence.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing personnel records and practical coaching support the task.
tasks.still_hard: Assessing judgment and helping a new manager handle unfamiliar situations.
tasks.human_edge: The manager explains expectations and adapts coaching to demonstrated needs.

reach.learn: Use explicit role evidence and practical coaching goals

evidence.claim: Human manager selection and coaching are an E1 design; scheduling products do not establish a saving in this task.

assumptions: This task covers associate-unit managers, distinct from general employee hiring and training.
The postal manager gathers candidate and learning evidence within s1 with all time retained; no free competence score is assumed.
Existing HCM and DOCS precede any new selection tool.
No new service or incremental upkeep is introduced.
unknowns: Selection authority and manager development arrangements
research_questions: Which practical management situations require the most follow-up coaching?

already_counted.description: Selection evidence review and practical management coaching

incremental.description: No added selection or coaching service

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 R=100 gives zero gross and net saving. General employee work is not counted a second time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Accountable postal operations and people leadership
reach: Work with operations analysts on consistent reporting
Learn evidence-based people practices from human resources specialists
role.ambitious_version: A postal manager who reduces repeated report assembly while preserving direct people leadership and negotiation
